## Contingent hypotheses

We specify four further hypotheses in full here, outside the confirmatory set, because each depends on a fact about the extract that the data controller has not yet confirmed. Each carries an activation rule, and the rule is a function of that fact alone.

A contingent hypothesis activates only if its condition is confirmed in writing by the data controller before this protocol is submitted, and the confirmation is reproduced in the supplementary material. A condition confirmed after submission does not activate anything: the hypothesis is then reported at Stage 2 as exploratory, under that label, and is not counted among the confirmatory tests. This asymmetry is deliberate, because a hypothesis activated after review has not been reviewed.

**C1. Coherence and inferential comprehension.** Condition: item-level comprehension responses exist and carry a recoverable question type. We would predict that, in an item-level model of response correctness, ReferentialContinuity × QuestionType is positive with inference questions coded 1 and literal questions 0, so that surface continuity helps more where the question requires integration [@freedAssessmentInferencemakingChildren2021; @pickrenContributionTextCharacteristics2022; @aparicioComprehensionPerformancesExplanatory2022].

**C2. Narration and comprehension.** Condition: item-level comprehension responses exist, and accounts are observed both with and without narration. We would predict that, within an account, narration is positively associated with response correctness after text, age band, reading level, accumulated reading and language are adjusted for. The expected size is small [@clintonlisellDoesReadingWhile2023; @woodUseTexttoSpeech2018], and the coefficient identifies an association and not an effect.

**C3. Reading pace and comprehension.** Condition: as C2, restricted to sessions without narration. We would predict that an account's mean log reading time per word is negatively associated with response correctness, so that accounts with a faster habitual pace answer more accurately [@sortkaerBothSidesStory2021]. The simultaneous within-account deviation term keeps this between-account association distinct from a difficult or interrupted session.

**C4. Machine-generated against human-authored text.** Condition: the classic stories are confirmed to be fixed, human-authored texts, identical for all users within a language. We would predict that the three text components predict reading pace with coefficients of the same sign and of comparable magnitude in generated and in classic texts, and that the interaction of each component with the generated-or-classic indicator is practically equivalent to zero. This is a test of exchangeability, not of quality. A non-negligible interaction would mean that the properties governing how children read human-written stories govern their reading of generated ones differently, which matters well beyond this platform.

## Randomisation, blinding and analytic independence

Nothing in this study is randomised. It is a secondary analysis of records generated by families using a commercial application, and no allocation, assignment or condition is under anyone's control. The only random assignment anywhere in the protocol is the permutation quality check, where we reassign texts to readings at random precisely to destroy the association under test.

Blinding is structural: we cannot see the outcome data because the data controller holds them, under the sequestration arrangement described above. We will write, run and debug the outcome-model code against data simulated from the design specification deposited with this protocol, so that every script is complete and exercised before the real file exists on any machine of ours.

{{< pagebreak >}}

# Conclusion

The trade this design makes is now explicit. It gives up experimental control, random assignment and any claim to a representative population, and it accepts an outcome measured once per story instead of once per fixation. In return it obtains hundreds to thousands of distinct texts as a random factor, ten or more languages, a number of readers per language beyond what a laboratory consortium can fund, and reading behaviour recorded where reading actually happens. We judge that trade worth making for this question in particular, because the question is whether text effects established under laboratory control survive outside it, and no better-controlled study can answer a question about what happens when control is absent.

The case does not rest on scale alone, and the design analysis is what keeps it honest. Precision here is governed by the number of distinct texts and not by the number of sessions, and sessions are the quantity this platform has in abundance. A very large export could therefore still leave the primary hypothesis underpowered, which is why every threshold in @tbl-design was fixed before the extract was released and why a hypothesis below its threshold will be declared underpowered before its model is fitted.

Each outcome is informative. If the three text coefficients are practically non-negligible, then the lexical, grammatical and discourse determinants of reading generalise from controlled settings to unsupervised, multilingual, machine-generated reading, which has not previously been shown. If they are practically equivalent to zero, that is a substantive negative result about the ecological reach of a large literature, obtained with precision the literature has not previously had. If the extract holds too few distinct texts, the protocol will say so before fitting and report that this platform cannot answer the question, which is itself worth knowing about a class of data source that others will be tempted to use.

The developmental hypotheses offer the clearest gain. No existing test of either interaction had more than 81 children, and the two accounts we register make opposite predictions on the scale this study uses. A determinate result in either direction adjudicates between them, and a posterior inside the region of practical equivalence would be evidence of absence rather than absence of evidence, which is a verdict no existing study has been large enough to deliver.

The limits should be equally clear. This study will not identify a causal effect of any text property, age band or narration setting. It will not estimate how fast children in general read, nor generalise beyond families who chose to install and use this application. It will say nothing about comprehension unless the contingent hypotheses activate on evidence that the necessary items exist. Where the data controller's answers falsify an auxiliary assumption, the affected predictions are reassigned by the rules in @tbl-unresolved, never reinterpreted after the fact.

More of children's reading is migrating to platforms that record it, and the question of whether such records can support inference will be asked repeatedly and answered badly if it is answered informally. This protocol is one worked attempt at answering it well: sequester the data until the analysis is reviewed, register every decision rule as a function of counts and not of coefficients, calculate in advance what the design can and cannot settle, and name the accounts that a determinate result would refute.

# Data and code availability

The session-level extract is held by the data controller and is not in our possession at submission. On in-principle acceptance it will be transferred under a data-sharing agreement between the University of Oxford and the data controller, whose terms govern what may subsequently be published. The story texts, the computed text features, the component scores, the fitted model objects and every table and figure underlying the reported results will be deposited on acceptance, to the extent the agreement permits. Where a field cannot be released, we will state the reason and deposit a derived form sufficient to reproduce the reported analyses. The provider-computed aggregate counts and the file manifest are deposited with this protocol, since they contain no record of any individual.

All analysis code is public and version-controlled. The theory object with its checks and derived diagram, the design specifications with the precision analysis, and the literature sizing are deposited with this protocol, so everything except the fitting of the models to real data can be reproduced now. The outcome-model code will be written against simulated data, as described above, and deposited before the extract is transferred. The four packages this protocol relies on are open source and archived: theoryforge for the theory object and its rigour scoring, pilotr for the design specification and the precision analysis, scopusflow for the literature sizing, and depictr for the figures [@bernabeuTheoryforge2026; @bernabeuPilotr2026; @bernabeuScopusflow2026; @bernabeuDepictr2026]. Each is cited by its concept identifier, and the archived releases hold the versions used here, which are also recorded in the session records deposited beside every output.
